📌 Tehran, IRNA – Parliament Speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says that the way out of the neither-war-nor-peace situation depends on achieving sustainable deterrence.

Achieving sustainable deterrence means we have become strong, and we must know its components in all fields, including the economy, politics, military, media, and social cohesion, and make them operational, Ghalibaf said, addressing the Omid Media Cup on Monday.
​
A strong Iran is what the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution emphasized, and the officials, and subsequently all the people, are tasked with strengthening Iran, and making science efficient and converting it into technology is one of the significant matters on this path, he added.
​
Today, the enemy has recognized that the people and Armed Forces will not withdraw under bombardment and intense fire, the official noted.
​
In this war, the number of bombs and the volume of fire used against Iran were greater than those used in the US’ 20-year war in Vietnam.
​
Stressing that the shadow of war cannot be removed from the country through diplomacy alone, he said that fighting alone cannot eliminate this threat either, because both diplomacy and war are instruments for achieving deterrence power.
​
Today, social integration is the most important element of our power against the enemy, and we must do everything in our power to preserve and strengthen it, Ghalibaf stated.
​
War today can make a major contribution to resolving the country’s economic, cultural, political, and other issues, but in these circumstances, we must tell the story correctly and not get sidetracked, he said.

📌 New York, IRNA – Iran’s Ambassador and Chargé d’Affaires to the United Nations in New York, Gholamhossein Darzi, has rejected Bahrain’s “baseless allegations” against Iran, saying the United States uses military bases across the region, including in Bahrain, to carry out its ongoing acts of aggression against Iran.

“The Islamic Republic of Iran categorically rejects these baseless allegations as a cynical attempt to grossly distort the facts and misrepresent Iran’s defensive measures, while deliberately concealing Bahrain’s undeniable role in facilitating and enabling the ongoing U.S. aggression against Iran,” the ambassador said in a letter dated November 23 and addressed to the UN Secretary-General and the president of the UN Security Council.
​
The letter was sent after Bahrain alleged that an Iranian attack had struck an industrial facility on Saturday, while Iran said it had launched a missile and drone assault on US military positions in the kingdom.
​
The following is the full text of the Iranian ambassador’s letter:
​
Upon instructions from my Government, and further to our previous letters regarding the continued internationally wrongful acts committed by the Kingdom of Bahrain through its complicity in, and facilitation of, the ongoing acts of aggression by the United States against the Islamic Republic of Iran, I wish to refer to the letters dated 16 and 19 November 2026 from the Permanent Representative of the Kingdom of Bahrain (S/2026/911 and S/2026/924) in which unfounded and repetitive allegations were levelled against the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Islamic Republic of Iran categorically rejects these baseless allegations as a cynical attempt to grossly distort the facts and misrepresent Iran's defensive measures, while deliberately concealing Bahrain's undeniable role in facilitating and enabling the ongoing U.S. aggression against Iran.
​
I wish to bring the following positions to the attention of the members of the Security Council:
​
1. The continued use of military bases and facilities in Persian Gulf region to plan, support and conduct U.S. acts of aggression against Iran: United States act of aggressions against the Islamic Republic of Iran continue unabated, in flagrant violation of Iran's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the fundamental principles of international law enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations. Most recently, on 2 and 17 November 2026, the United States carried out a series of military airstrikes against Iran's southern coastal areas along the Persian Gulf, in Hormozgan Province, targeting Iranian facilities and installations on Qeshm Island and in the vicinity of Sirik. On 20 November, an attack was carried out against a radar installation on Hengam Island. In response, on 21 November 2026, the Islamic Republic of Iran targeted the source of the attack in Bahrain. The intended target was the U.S. radar system located in the U.S. military's Sheikh Isa Base in Bahrain. Any alleged error in targeting was attributable solely to jamming operations and electronic warfare activities conducted by U.S. forces, which Bahrain hosts on its territory.
​
Credible information and evidence indicate that U.S. military drones, and other military assets, have been used in acts of aggression against Iran from military bases in the region, including in Bahrain and Kuwait.
